### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/client`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **38** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/api.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**24** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6e11a929e453e1f9a78a9eb7b311c46b2fa8d094`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/api.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `responseSchema (6 routes)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6e11a929e453e1f9a78a9eb7b311c46b2fa8d094` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e3988a17151edfb49ba4cd97a1263b0464629647` — the merge of head `387e88ca7346efc317c9e5993b3ebe0b9170f375` into base `6e11a929e453e1f9a78a9eb7b311c46b2fa8d094`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e3988a17151edfb49ba4cd97a1263b0464629647 && git checkout e3988a17151edfb49ba4cd97a1263b0464629647
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6e11a929e453e1f9a78a9eb7b311c46b2fa8d094 387e88ca7346efc317c9e5993b3ebe0b9170f375 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6e11a929e453e1f9a78a9eb7b311c46b2fa8d094 && git merge --no-ff 387e88ca7346efc317c9e5993b3ebe0b9170f375

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6e11a929e453e1f9a78a9eb7b311c46b2fa8d094
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6e11a929e453e1f9a78a9eb7b311c46b2fa8d094` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

The accept set and public face the diff moves, each judged:

1. **New request schema `CloneFlowRequestSchema`** (`@objectstack/spec/api`): `z.object({ name, label, package? }).strict()`, `name`/`label` `string().min(1)`, `package` `string().min(1).optional()`, each with a `describe` naming the refusal it draws (409 taken name; 422 `WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED` / 409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` on a bad target; 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` on `package` when omitted for a source no read-only package ships). 2. **The door honours the schema's member set.** `handleAutomationRequest`'s clone arm now derives `declaredKeys` from `CloneFlowRequestSchema.shape` and refuses any other key 400 `unknown_field` on that key, so door and declaration cannot disagree on the closed set; the contract suite's "an undeclared one is refused on its key" case pins it. The one residual: the door refuses a whitespace-only `package` (`trim() === ''`, 400 `invalid_type`) where `min(1)` would accept it. That is the door being one notch stricter than its declaration on a value no caller means; noted, not a defect in the accept set a consumer relies on.
3. **New response schema `CloneFlowResponseSchema`** = `BaseResponseSchema.extend({ data: { flow: FlowSchema, packageId: string, notice: string } })`. The whole envelope is named, as the uninstall row's is. The door answers `deps.success({ flow: servedFlowDefinition(clone), packageId: target.packageId, notice: FLOW_CLONE_NOTICE })`; the new suite parses every 200 through this schema. **Correct.** `packageId` is the new member; `flow` and `notice` are unchanged. There was no response schema before (the row was `server-only`); it now exists and the ledger row names both schemas.
4. **Accept-to-refuse moves, exactly:** (a) a clone of a source that no read-only package ships (an environment flow, or one stored in a writable package), sent without `package`: 200 package-less before, now `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` with `fields: [{ field: 'package', code: 'required' }]`, nothing registered or stored. (b) a clone of a packaged source whose base cannot be paired (the ensure door's own 404/409 refusals, relayed as thrown, e.g. a base with no namespace) — before, package-less 200. (c) nothing else moves from accept to refuse: the taken-name 409, credential 409, walled refusal, `manage_metadata` 403, anonymous 401 and unknown-source 404 are untouched, and a packaged source with no `package` still answers 200 (now landing in the pair). The refusal families are existing ones only: `VALIDATION_FAILED` (the validation-failure kit), `WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED` (the save door's own, `uninstalledNamedBaseRefusal` / `isWritablePackage`) and `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`. `DUPLICATE_SOURCE_NOT_A_BASE` is correctly **not** reused: the order asked for its family "unless the code's meaning doesn't fit (then say why)"; it names a bad SOURCE and every refusal here is about the TARGET; the dev said so on the PR and kept that family's shape (`[tag]` sentence, `details.packageId`, `details.docs`). No new code is minted. **Correct.**
5. **Default target.** `package` omitted → `protocol.packagedArtifactOwner({ type: 'flow', name })` (the loader's set, never the engine's `_packageId` stamp) names the base → `protocol.ensureCustomizationPackage({ basePackageId })` returns the pair → the pair is then judged by the same target rule. Read in `protocol-customization-package.ts`: the ensure body is idempotent (an existing pair is returned unchanged or refused naming what it lacks, never adopted or rewritten), per-pair in-flight calls are serialised, a writable base is refused 409, an unknown base 404. **In-process, the one creation path, idempotent reuse** — pinned by "a second clone reuses the pair" (one installed pair, no second persist). Correct.
6. **Explicit target.** `newSimilarTargetRefusal`: not installed → 422 `WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED`; `!isWritablePackage` → 422; writable but `resolvePackageClosure(target).dependencies` lacks the source's package → 409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`. The closure walk is `@objectstack/lint/runtime`'s, the same one `protocol-write-package-scope.ts` (the save door's publish gate) uses; `@objectstack/lint` does not depend on `@objectstack/runtime`, so the new `workspace:*` dependency in `packages/runtime/package.json` introduces no cycle (the lockfile hunk is the matching link). Refusals are answered before anything is registered; the table case pins `registerFlow` not called, no row, no pair minted. Correct.
7. **Copy inactive, original unchanged, no double-run.** `FLOW_CLONE_STATUS` moves `'draft'` → `'obsolete'`; the engine disables only on `obsolete`/`invalid` (its `registerFlow`), so `draft` armed exactly like `active` — the measured double-run on showcase. Pinned: the answer, the stored row and the registered flow all read `obsolete`; the source stays `active` with no row written under its name. The card's literal word was "draft"; the card's **intent** ("so a clone never double-runs beside its original") is only met by `obsolete`, and the dev stated the deviation on the PR. Judged correct; the seat may wish to amend the card's wording when closing it.
8. **No base envelope on the copy.** `cloneFlowDefinition` still drops `_packageId`, `_packageVersion`, `_provenance`, `_lock`; the save carries `packageId: target` as a save parameter (the row's `package_id` binding), not as a stamp on the item. Pinned: the answer has none of the four keys; the row's item `_packageId` is not the base and `_provenance` is not `'package'`. The dogfood provenance fixture's flipped assertion (`isCodeArtifactBody(served.doc)` now true) is the `/meta` read surfacing the row's binding as `_packageId: pair` — the same served shape the file already measures for `META_BOUND`, and the fixture now also proves the copy's round-trip PUT into the pair saves 200. That is the pair's binding, not the base's envelope. Correct.
9. **First-write pin.** The clone's `saveMetaItem` carries `parentVersion: null`; a `409 METADATA_CONFLICT` from the store is translated by `flowWriteRefusal` into the clone door's own taken-name 409 with its remedy. A row the target already holds under the name (one the engine's collision probe cannot see) is never overwritten. Correct, and a sound tightening.

Correct.

The view test pins the href starts with `/studio/{encoded packageId}/automations`, not `/studio/~org`, plus the no-link control. Correct.

Landing still waits on a fully green head per the seat's ② rule; nothing in this diff is implicated.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev `open_questions`: none. Dev-flagged judgement calls, both answered above: `obsolete` not `draft` (①.7, accepted); refusal codes not `DUPLICATE_SOURCE_NOT_A_BASE` (①.4, accepted).

### ④ Design judgment

- **`packages/spec/src/api/automation-api.zod.ts`** against the ruling and its first consumer. The ruling (epic #28236, Q6, "clone kept only as new similar, landing in the paired `.custom`"; ADR-0146 D3/D4; ADR-0070 D5/D6 retiring the package-less scope) is what the schema declares: a closed body, an optional `package` whose describe text states both the default (the pair, ensured on first use) and the one case with no default (a source no read-only package ships), and a response that names where the copy landed.
